doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

chapter: Early road bands and the Army
title: Avoiding the draft, Frankie Carle's band and induction
summary: City College study delayed the draft; after the Kenton offer fell through he joined Frankie Carle, then was inducted in 1957.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yes. Did the prospect of the draft frighten you?

Well it did. Actually I’ll take a minute and a half and tell you this story. I’m trying to think of the timeframe. I went to City College actually because I wanted to go to City College, but probably a lesser reason was that the Korean War was going on then too and I really didn’t want to go for that. So I couldn’t just go to City College and take music. You had to prepare for a teacher’s credential to make it legitimate. So to do that I had to take a lot of subjects that I had had a bellyful of in high school like English and sciences and history and things that really didn’t interest me at all but I did it because I wanted that education, because I really didn’t want to go to Korea. But my grades were so bad in the academic subjects that they finally flunked me out and I went on the road in 1954, and just stayed out of school and figured I’d take my chances. And then I got a call from Bill Perkins in San Francisco. He was on Stan’s band then, and he said would you like to come on the band, Lennie Niehaus is going to leave. And I said I’d love to, because that’s the band that Bill Holman was writing for, and I ate and slept that band, it was a wonderful band. And I said yes. And he said well just sit tight, it shouldn’t be too long. Well he called in another month and said Lennie’s decided to stay for a while. In the meantime I had to make some money so I joined Frankie Carle’s band. Remember that band?

Well there was a three-month tour with that band to mostly the southwest. And I went on that tour and we were playing Texas A&M and a cadet came up with a note from my parents and it said, “Lanny call home regarding induction notice.”

So they gave me a couple of months to finish the tour and settle my affairs, and then I went in the Army I think March ’57 and then I got out New Year’s Eve in 1958. So it took a big chunk out which I regretted. I mean I think something could have happened to my career faster had I had that opportunity then. But actually my time in the service was mostly in Europe with the Seventh Army Symphony and we played a couple of soldier shows which are like Broadway shows that they send around to the different Kacernes
